title: Design an LLM Inference Serving System
prompt: Design a serving system that runs a large language model behind an API: it accepts a stream of user requests (each a prompt, wanting streamed token-by-token output) and returns generated tokens with low latency, using a fixed pool of GPUs efficiently.
requirements: Functional: accept generation requests with prompts and parameters, stream tokens back as they're generated, support many concurrent requests per GPU
Non-functional: low time-to-first-token, high aggregate throughput (tokens/sec across the GPU fleet), must not let one huge request starve others
discussion_points: Continuous/dynamic batching of requests with different prompt lengths and arrival times onto the same GPU
KV-cache management: memory budget per GPU, eviction when the cache fills up, and reuse across requests sharing a prefix
Scheduling policy across GPUs (which request goes where) and fairness between a short chat request and a long completion
Autoscaling the GPU fleet based on queue depth/load, and cold-start cost of loading model weights
Where request queuing and backpressure live when the fleet is saturated
How streaming output is delivered back to clients (chunked HTTP, SSE, WebSockets) without blocking the generation loop
